question: Superfecundation occurs when a second pregnancy develops in a woman who is already pregnant, resulting in two foetuses of very different gestational ages in the same uterus.

l10n.wrongAnswerMessage: Incorrect. Superfecundation = fertilisation of two ova from the same cycle by sperm from different occasions (possibly different fathers) — relevant in paternity disputes. Superfoetation = pregnancy occurring during an existing pregnancy (two foetuses of very different gestational ages) — extremely rare and primarily a biological curiosity. Do not confuse the two.
l10n.correctAnswerMessage: Correct — this is false. What you have described is superfoetation (fertilisation of a second ovum during an existing pregnancy — extremely rare). Superfecundation is the fertilisation of two ova released in the same ovulatory cycle by sperm from separate acts of intercourse — potentially from different men (heteropaternal superfecundation). The two are distinct phenomena with different medicolegal implications.
